report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1 of daedalus/lanes/fanout.py; enumerated all docstring claims; most are uncheckable or kept within this window; no broken claims cited.
risks: fanout.py:1-149 | medium | Module docstring makes several claims about behaviour outside this chunk (guard installation, provider internals, atomic writes, render_brief semantics) that are uncheckable here; downstream readers may assume them without verification. | Read the rest of the file and referenced modules.

fanout.py:55-75 | medium | FanoutTask.key docstring claims collision-free and filename-safe, but the sanitisation logic is fully in this chunk; the hash is only 10 hex chars (40 bits), so collision-free is not mathematically guaranteed. | Assess whether 40-bit collision risk is acceptable for the resume identity.

fanout.py:89-112 | medium | FanoutResult.blocked claims to detect refusals via report.status == 'blocked', but the shape of 'report' is not defined in this chunk; if the provider changes shape, blocked may silently misreport. | Check provider output schema and tests.

fanout.py:120-149 | medium | _one_call docstring claims policy is passed to classify_data and that DeepSeekProvider applies secret_floor_rule; both are outside this chunk. The temperature default 0.0 is visible here, but the enforcement of temperature > 0 for votes > 1 is not in this chunk. | Read the rest of the file and the provider.

fanout.py:1-149 | medium | The flight recorder records digests of the objective and system override, but the actual prompt sent is not recorded; if the brief or provider modifies the objective further, the digest may not match what was sent. | Verify provider.run does not alter objective after this point.

handoff.purpose: Defines FanoutTask, FanoutResult, default_concurrency, and _one_call; sets module-level constants and extensive design rationale.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY
symbols.note: Module-level constant set to 8; documented as measured concurrency ceiling.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_S
symbols.note: Module-level constant set to 300; documented as per-call ceiling.

symbols.name: default_concurrency
symbols.note: Reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY env var; returns max(1, int(raw)) if raw else DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY; on ValueError returns DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.

symbols.name: FanoutTask
symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with task_id, objective, paths, votes, meta; property key derives a filename-safe identity.

symbols.name: FanoutTask.key
symbols.note: Property; sanitises task_id, collapses dots, truncates to 80 chars, appends 10-hex SHA256 digest.

symbols.name: FanoutResult
symbols.note: Dataclass with task_id, key, votes_requested, answers, errors, meta, resumed, trace_id; properties ok and blocked; method to_dict.

symbols.name: FanoutResult.blocked
symbols.note: Property; returns True if all answers have report.status == 'blocked'.

symbols.name: FanoutResult.to_dict
symbols.note: Returns dict with task_id, key, trace_id, votes_requested, votes_collected, answers, errors, meta.

symbols.name: _one_call
symbols.note: Imports DeepSeekProvider, builds objective with brief, instantiates provider, calls provider.run with writable=False, returns dict with vote, provider, persona, report, notes, sent digest info.

claims.text: The volume half of the two-judge plan. Its one job is to run N advisory tasks through the DeepSeek lane at bounded concurrency and land each answer on disk as its own file, so that 1,200 tasks are a *queue* rather than an *event* -- a crash at task 900 costs one task, not nine hundred.
claims.why: The chunk defines the task dataclass and one-call helper but does not contain the fan_out function or the disk-writing logic; those are in the rest of the file.

claims.text: Every design choice here is a measured failure from 29/30 July.
claims.why: This is a historical claim about measurements not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The fan-out scripts that night constructed the provider directly and never called daedalus.budget.install_process_guard, so ~170 paid calls left the machine unpriced before anyone noticed. The guard is not optional here and not a parameter -- a fan-out is exactly the shape that turns a missing guard into a bill.
claims.why: The chunk does not show installation of the guard; that would be in fan_out or module top-level, not in this window.

claims.text: CORROBORATION IS THE POINT, NOT A FEATURE. That night produced 1,226 claims whose largest agreement cluster was TWO, because the fan-out handed every agent a different file. N agents on N different things cannot corroborate anything; N agents on the SAME thing can. So votes is a first-class argument and every result records how many independent answers it is made of.
claims.why: The chunk shows votes is a field on FanoutTask and FanoutResult records votes_requested, but the claim about the historical incident and the fan_out function's behaviour is outside this chunk.

claims.text: AND votes NEEDS temperature > 0, which is enforced rather than documented. ... fan_out now REFUSES the combination.
claims.why: The chunk shows _one_call has a temperature parameter defaulting to 0.0, but the refusal logic is in fan_out, which is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A FRESH PROVIDER PER CALL. DeepSeekProvider.run resets self._written per call precisely so one instance cannot report a prior call's writes as this one's. Sharing an instance across worker threads would reintroduce that race by another door, so each call gets its own.
claims.why: In _one_call, line ~138, a new DeepSeekProvider() is instantiated per call, as claimed.

claims.text: THE GRAPH GOES IN THE PROMPT. No provider module referenced structcore until 2026-07-30; the entire context a lane received was raw file bytes, and three of seven agent-written modules imported things that do not exist. Tasks that name paths get daedalus.lanes.graph_brief.render_brief prepended.
claims.why: The chunk imports render_brief and _one_call accepts a brief parameter and prepends it to the objective before the question.

claims.text: RESULTS ARE PUBLISHED, NOT WRITTEN. Via daedalus.atomic, so a reader tailing the output directory during a four-hour run never sees half a JSON document.
claims.why: The chunk imports write_text_atomic but does not show where results are written; that is in fan_out.

claims.text: Advisory only. There is no writable parameter and adding one would be a mistake: a write lane needs daedalus.lanes.checks.run_checks around every file and a rollback story per task, and a fan-out has neither. Volume and writes do not belong in the same primitive.
claims.why: In _one_call, provider.run is called with writable=False, and the FanoutTask dataclass has no writable field.

claims.text: Concurrency ceiling. The lane is network-bound, so this is far above the core count -- but not unbounded: each worker holds a provider, a request and a response body, and the box also has to keep running whatever else is on it. MEASURED 2026-07-30: a hundred concurrent agents pushed the test suite past a 900 s timeout, and the gate read that timeout as failing tests. The suite is 4,146 tests and 765 s on this box when idle -- NOT the 105 s the handoff carried, which is a stale figure and the reason 18 minutes per gate mutation looked mysterious. If a measurement is running, pass a low number and mean it.
claims.why: The measurement claim is historical and not verifiable from this chunk; the constant is set to 8.

claims.text: Concurrency from the environment, or DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY.
claims.why: The function reads DAEDALUS_FANOUT_CONCURRENCY and falls back to DEFAULT_CONCURRENCY on empty or invalid input.

claims.text: One question, asked votes times independently.
claims.why: FanoutTask has a votes field; the independence is enforced elsewhere (temperature), but the dataclass supports multiple votes.

claims.text: key is the filename the answer lands under and the resume identity, so it must be stable across runs and safe as a path segment. It is derived from task_id rather than trusted, because a task id built from a commit message or a file path will contain separators.
claims.why: The key property derives from task_id by sanitising and appending a digest; it is deterministic and filename-safe.

claims.text: A filename-safe, collision-free, stable identity.
claims.why: Filename-safe and stable are checkable in this chunk; collision-free is not guaranteed because the digest is only 10 hex chars (40 bits), so collisions are possible, though extremely unlikely. The claim is too strong for this implementation, but the practical risk is negligible.

claims.text: The digest is appended rather than the sanitised name being trusted: a/b and a\b both sanitise to a_b, and two tasks sharing a result file would have one silently overwrite the other's answer.
claims.why: The sanitisation replaces both '/' and '\' with '_' (since they are not alnum or in '-_.'), so both become 'a_b'; the digest differentiates them.

claims.text: Dot runs are collapsed after sanitising. Replacing separators already makes traversal impossible, but ../../etc/passwd still produced .._.._etc_passwd -- a key that cannot escape and reads as though it were trying to. A name that looks like an attack invites someone to 'harden' it later by a route that breaks resume.
claims.why: The code collapses '..' repeatedly and strips leading dots/underscores; the example '.._.._etc_passwd' would be collapsed to '_etc_passwd' after the while loop and lstrip.

claims.text: True when this result was loaded from disk rather than paid for again.
claims.why: The field exists but the loading logic is in fan_out, not this chunk.

claims.text: From daedalus.spine.envelope.current_trace_id, which NEVER mints -- so None means 'no trace was in scope', not 'here is a fresh unrelated id'.
claims.why: The trace_id field exists but its assignment is in fan_out; the behaviour of current_trace_id is in another module.

claims.text: Present because the drift detector in tests/test_envelope_coverage.py caught this module as an undeclared record producer on 2026-07-30 and it was right: these files record a PAID external call and its answer, so a trace id correlates a bill to the run that incurred it. That is the join anyone reconstructing a spend six months later needs, and its absence is exactly the 'new island' the detector exists to prevent.
claims.why: Historical and cross-module claim; not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Every collected answer is a refusal.
claims.why: The property returns True only if all answers are dicts with report dicts having status == 'blocked'.

claims.text: ok answers 'did the transport produce answers'; this answers 'did any of them carry evidence'. The distinction was measured 2026-07-31 on the claims123 review tier: 6 of 6 units came back with report.status == 'blocked' and the run summary said ok=6 -- an audit that audited nothing, reported as if it had. A unit with at least one non-blocked answer stays un-blocked, because partial evidence is evidence.
claims.why: The property returns True only if all answers have status 'blocked'; if any answer is non-blocked, it returns False, matching the claim.

claims.text: One advisory call. Returns the answer dict; raises on transport failure.
claims.why: The function returns a dict, but whether it raises on transport failure depends on provider.run, which is outside this chunk.

claims.text: policy is handed to the provider, which passes it to daedalus.sensitivity.classify_data. Default None means the project's own policy applies -- so a caller that never heard of this argument gets the fence it already had, and widening egress is something an operator does on purpose at the call site rather than a default anybody inherits.
claims.why: The policy argument is passed to provider.run, but the claim about classify_data is in the provider module.

claims.text: It cannot lift the secret floor. providers/deepseek.py calls secret_floor_rule per path independently of classify_data, and that rule is documented as running 'in EVERY lane, no bypass ... cannot be weakened by a project config'. Verified with a fully permissive policy: source files pass, .env is still refused.
claims.why: This claim is about the provider module and secret_floor_rule, which are outside this chunk.

claims.text: Imported here, not at module scope: this module is imported by tooling that must not pull the provider stack (and its network config) just to read the dataclasses.
claims.why: The import of DeepSeekProvider is inside the function body, as claimed.

claims.text: BEFORE the question, not after. A model that has already read the question treats the brief as supporting material; a model that reads the brief first treats the question as being about the thing described.
claims.why: The code prepends the brief to the objective before the task text.

claims.text: fresh per call -- see module docstring
claims.why: Provider is instantiated inside _one_call, so each call gets a new instance.

claims.text: temperature >0 is what makes votes independent
claims.why: The temperature is passed to provider.run, but the claim that >0 makes votes independent is a property of the provider's sampling, not verifiable here.

claims.text: writable=False, advisory only, structurally
claims.why: provider.run is called with writable=False.

observations.what: FanoutTask.key uses only 10 hex chars of SHA256 (40 bits) for collision resistance; the docstring claims 'collision-free', which is mathematically not guaranteed, though practically extremely unlikely.

The module docstring claims the fan-out lands each answer on disk as its own file, but this chunk does not contain any disk-writing code; the write_text_atomic import suggests it is in fan_out, which is in the next chunk.

The temperature default is 0.0 in _one_call, but the module docstring says fan_out refuses votes > 1 with temperature 0. That refusal is not in this chunk; if it is missing in the next chunk, the claim would be broken.

The flight recorder records objective_sha256 and system_override_sha256, but the actual prompt sent may differ if the provider further modifies the objective; the digest is of the local objective, not necessarily what was sent.
